body:
something which the previous version also doesn't implement yet, and thus could be done in a separate PR, is adding `queryID` & absolute position to the hits array so it can be used for insights, like it can for Hits & InfiniteHits; cc @tkrugg 

see also https://github.com/algolia/react-instantsearch/pull/2687
We don't have to repeat the type inside the name, the information is already carried by the type.
We could print the alternative usage WDYT?
The function should read from the previous parameter then fallback.
The return value should be `void` we don't have to expose the Helper through the connector.
We could add a comment that explain why we mutate the results.
For which cases the value is `undefined`?
We can already name it `indexName`.

We don't really showcase the full power of the connector. IMO we should use the `refine` behaviour of the connector, rather than relying on the `searchBox` (for the design we can give it the same class).
We can add the `widgetParams` and `instantSearchInstance` to the test.

```suggestion
    const widget = makeWidget();
```

It doesn't make sense to add the option for test, we don't use it.
We should create a mock helper for this we do it thousand times across the codebase.
The widget does not implement the routing lifecycle, we can add them in a separate PR though.
Those types are a nightmare to follow, would be nice to simplify them at some point. No idea how though.

This is needed otherwise we cannot do this assertion:

```ts
expect(secondRenderOptions.indices[0].hits).toEqual(firstIndexHits);
```

Because we add `__escaped`, to the array with `escapeHTML` to `true`. Jest considers them as different arrays.
WDYM? A link to the doc?
None, it's mistyped.
We mutate the results also in `connectHits` and `connectInfiniteHits`. What kind of comment would you expect?
What could we showcase more with the search box connector that we don't with the widget?
Let's do it in another PR.

Convert the usage of `indices` into `index` This what we did for [the `geoSearch` warnings](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/509513c0feafaad522f6f18d87a441559f4aa050/src/connectors/geo-search/connectGeoSearch.js#L117-L132).
Yes we do, but it's not obvious why we do it. Something that mention highlighting.

The story do not use `refine`, `currentRefinement` to implement the autocomplete. We leverage the `searchBox` widget. Most of the time people will build their autocomplete with the connector only, specially if it's an integration with a pre-built component. IMO it worth showcasing the full API.
My bad.
This is fine, but we should probably avoid calling state functions multiple times, and can join them all in a single setQueryParameters, WDYT?
Do we want to support previous highlighting tags?
Do we keep `indices` or rename it to `items` like the other widgets?

We do that in other connectors. They don't mutate the global state, they return a new object.
Why would you recommend not calling these functions multiple times?
I don't think so, otherwise it might break our highlighting feature.
`items` refers most of the time to a list of facet values, `hits` refers to a list of hits, `indices` could make sense. Both are valid, I don't think it matters much.
